catalyst_text: Positive two year CAHtalyst results presented at ENDO
detailed_catalyst_text: Two‑year outcomes from the adult and pediatric Phase 3 CAHtalyst program in classic congenital adrenal hyperplasia due to 21‑hydroxylase deficiency were presented at ENDO 2026. Presentations highlighted sustained decreases in glucocorticoid doses and other favorable long‑term clinical measures, adding to the post‑approval evidence base.

catalyst_text: Presented positive two year pediatric Phase 3 results
detailed_catalyst_text: New two-year Phase 3 pediatric data in classic congenital adrenal hyperplasia were presented at ENDO 2026, showing slowed bone age progression and improved predicted adult height in children with advanced bone age at baseline. The findings suggest sustained androgen control with reduced glucocorticoid exposure may positively influence growth outcomes in pediatric patients.
catalyst_text_evidence: SAN DIEGO, 2026-06-15 /PRNewswire/ -- Neurocrine Biosciences, Inc. (NASDAQ:NBIX) today announced new two-year data from the Phase 3 CAHtalyst Pediatric study showing positive growth outcomes in children and adolescents with classic congenital adrenal hyperplasia treated with CRENESSITY (crinecerfont). These data were presented at the Endocrine Society's annual meeting, ENDO 2026, in Chicago. Among those with advanced bone age at baseline (n=24), bone age SDS remained stable or improved in most patients with up to two years of CRENESSITY treatment. Mean bone age SDS decreased by 1.12, with a subset of patients (n=9) demonstrating reductions greater than two standard deviations. In this subset of patients, mean predicted adult height increased by 4.7 cm from baseline.

drug_indication: Classic Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia due to 11β-hydroxylase deficiency
catalyst_text: Positive case series results presented at ENDO 2026
detailed_catalyst_text: Initial real‑world clinical findings in patients with classic congenital adrenal hyperplasia due to 11β‑hydroxylase deficiency were presented, showing marked hormonal improvements and treatment de‑intensification. Results included large reductions in steroid precursors and androstenedione, glucocorticoid dose reductions in most patients, and reduced antihypertensive use in some adults, supporting use in this rare CAH subtype.
catalyst_text_evidence: Neurocrine Biosciences, Inc. (NASDAQ:NBIX) today announced clinical findings from the first retrospective case series in pediatric and adult patients with classic congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH) due to 11β‑hydroxylase deficiency. The findings were presented at the Endocrine Society's annual meeting, ENDO 2026, in Chicago. Androstenedione and other adrenal hormone levels in 11β‑hydroxylase-deficient patients improved substantially after initiation of CRENESSITY, with >90% median reductions in 11-deoxycortisol and 11-deoxycorticosterone. Nearly all patients (14/15) reduced their total glucocorticoid dose with CRENESSITY, and 2 of 5 patients on antihypertensive medications reduced or discontinued these drugs.

catalyst_text: Presented positive randomized withdrawal data at ENDO 2026
detailed_catalyst_text: New late-breaking clinical results were presented at ENDO 2026 from the Phase 3 program and long-term extension in Prader-Willi syndrome, including a randomized withdrawal re-treatment analysis. Patients who restarted therapy after withdrawal showed rapid and durable improvements in hyperphagia and behaviors, and continuous treatment maintained benefits, with additional comparative analyses versus a natural history cohort supporting sustained long-term efficacy. These findings strengthen evidence for durable management of hyperphagia in this population.
catalyst_text_evidence: SAN DIEGO, 2026-06-15 /PRNewswire/ -- Soleno Therapeutics, a Neurocrine Biosciences (NASDAQ:NBIX) company, today announced late-breaking data at ENDO 2026 showing that resuming treatment with VYKAT XR (diazoxide choline) extended-release tablets for two years after a 16-week randomized withdrawal period was associated with durable improvements in hyperphagia and behavioral symptoms characteristic of Prader-Willi syndrome (PWS). These data show that participants who resumed VYKAT XR after randomized withdrawal experienced recovery of treatment benefit, while those who continued therapy maintained durable improvements in hyperphagia and other PWS-related behaviors. A poster presentation led by Evelien F. Gevers, M.D., Ph.D., Barts Health NHS Trust/Queen Mary University of London, reported three-year data comparing 125 VYKAT XR-treated participants from Studies C601 and C602-OLE to 229 natural history controls from the PATH for PWS Natural History Study. VYKAT XR demonstrated statistically significant and sustained improvements in hyperphagia compared with the PATH cohort at all evaluated time points (p<0.0001), with treatment differences of 6.2 points at Year 1, 6.5 points at Year 2, and 6.2 points at Year 3 on the HQ-CT Total Score. A second presentation by Dr. Gevers reported PWSP data comparing 105 VYKAT XR-treated participants to 182 PATH controls over three years. Statistically significant improvements favoring VYKAT XR compared with the PATH cohort were observed across all six behavioral domains at Year 1 (p<0.001), Year 2 (p<0.01), and Year 3 (p<0.001).

catalyst_text: Presented positive Phase 3 two year data
detailed_catalyst_text: Two-year Phase 3 CAHtalyst Adult results were presented at ENDO 2026, showing sustained glucocorticoid dose reductions with improvements in weight, BMI, body composition, and insulin resistance in adults with classic congenital adrenal hyperplasia. Additional presentations reported favorable trends in bone mineral density and meaningful patient-reported quality of life outcomes, and pediatric two-year analyses were also shared. These findings add long-term evidence supporting disease management in this indication.
catalyst_text_evidence: SAN DIEGO, 2026-06-15 /PRNewswire/ -- Neurocrine Biosciences, Inc. (NASDAQ:NBIX) today announced new Phase 3 CAHtalyst Adult study data demonstrating improved cardiometabolic outcomes alongside sustained glucocorticoid dose reduction through up to two years of treatment with CRENESSITY (crinecerfont) for classic congenital adrenal hyperplasia. These results, together with additional presentations highlighting improvement in bone outcomes and patient-reported quality of life survey outcomes, were presented at the Endocrine Society's annual meeting, ENDO 2026, in Chicago. Sustained improvements were observed, with mean reductions from baseline in body weight, BMI and insulin resistance. Favorable trends in bone health outcomes were observed with CRENESSITY treatment, including improvements in bone mineral density with up to two years of treatment. Patient‑reported survey data from adults in the open-label extension suggested improvements in quality of life outcomes and treatment satisfaction, including emotional well‑being, energy levels and confidence in managing their classic congenital adrenal hyperplasia with CRENESSITY.

catalyst_text: Presented positive clinician reported data in tardive dyskinesia
detailed_catalyst_text: Clinician-reported real-world data in individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities and tardive dyskinesia were presented, showing rapid and meaningful reductions in movement severity after treatment initiation. Nearly all patients improved, with 89% improving within four weeks, and clinicians reported functional gains across daily living domains in 96% of those with baseline impairment. These findings support benefit in an underrepresented population and reinforce improvements in functional and socio-emotional outcomes.
catalyst_text_evidence: Neurocrine Biosciences, Inc. (Nasdaq: NBIX) today announced new clinician-reported data in patients with intellectual and developmental disabilities demonstrating meaningful and rapid improvements in tardive dyskinesia severity, as well as improvements in overall functional status, including physical and socio-emotional outcomes, with INGREZZA® (valbenazine) capsules. The findings were presented at the American Academy of Developmental Medicine and Dentistry's 24th Annual Education Conference in Dallas. Nearly all individuals experienced reductions in TD symptoms, with 89% (25/28) demonstrating improvement within four weeks of treatment initiation. Following treatment with INGREZZA, clinicians reported improvement in overall functional status in 96% of study participants with impaired function, as well as broad improvements across key aspects of daily life.

catalyst_text: Presented positive Phase 3 post hoc analysis results
detailed_catalyst_text: New post-hoc results from the open-label Phase 3 KINECT 4 study in adults with tardive dyskinesia demonstrated robust and clinically meaningful reductions in involuntary movement severity after 48 weeks of treatment. Among those not meeting symptomatic remission at Week 48, 86% achieved at least a 30% AIMS reduction and 67% achieved at least a 50% reduction, with approximately 94% overall achieving remission or a clinically meaningful response. These findings support durable efficacy across a broad patient population.
catalyst_text_evidence: Neurocrine Biosciences, Inc. (Nasdaq: NBIX) today announced new post-hoc data from the KINECT® 4 clinical trial demonstrating that adults with tardive dyskinesia (TD) treated with INGREZZA® (valbenazine) capsules experienced clinically meaningful and robust improvements in involuntary movement severity, including those who did not meet the stringent symptomatic remission threshold. These results, together with findings from a large retrospective Medicare claims analysis evaluating hepatic risk factors among patients newly diagnosed with TD, were presented at the 2026 Psych Congress Elevate in Las Vegas. A new post-hoc analysis further demonstrated that clinically meaningful improvements were observed even among patients who did not meet the more stringent symptomatic remission threshold. Among the 41% of patients (42/103) who did not meet the symptomatic remission threshold at Week 48, 86% (36/42) achieved ≥30% total AIMS score reduction (characterized by the authors as clinically meaningful), and 67% (28/42) achieved ≥50% reduction. This new analysis demonstrates that approximately 94% of patients treated with INGREZZA for 48 weeks either achieved symptomatic remission or experienced clinically meaningful reductions in their tardive dyskinesia movements.

catalyst_text: Presented positive real world data in tardive dyskinesia
detailed_catalyst_text: New clinician-survey real-world data in adults with mild tardive dyskinesia were presented at the American Psychiatric Association 2026 Annual Meeting, showing rapid and broad improvements after treatment. Clinicians reported 96% improved uncontrolled movements with 86% improving within four weeks, along with gains in functional status, independence, daily activities, and ability to work. These findings support treatment consideration even in mild cases based on associated impairment or patient preference.
catalyst_text_evidence: SAN DIEGO, 2026-05-18 /PRNewswire/ -- Neurocrine Biosciences, Inc. (Nasdaq: NBIX) today announced the presentation of new data from a clinician survey highlighting the functional impact experienced by patients with mild tardive dyskinesia (TD) severity and the impact of treatment with INGREZZA (valbenazine) capsules in a real-world setting. The findings are being presented at the American Psychiatric Association 2026 Annual Meeting, taking place 2026-05-16 to 2026-05-20 in San Francisco. Following the initiation of INGREZZA, nearly all patients (96%) with mild TD experienced clinician-reported improvements in uncontrolled movements. Of those patients, 86% improved in four weeks or less.

catalyst_text: Initiated Phase 1 trial initial data expected 2027
detailed_catalyst_text: A first-in-human Phase 1 study was initiated to evaluate safety and tolerability of a CRF2 agonist in adults with healthy weight, overweight, or obesity. This marks the start of clinical development for an obesity therapy targeting fat reduction with lean mass preservation.
catalyst_text_evidence: Neurocrine Biosciences, Inc. (NASDAQ:NBIX) today announced the initiation of a Phase 1 first-in-human clinical study evaluating the safety and tolerability of NBIP-'2118 in adult participants. NBIP-'2118 is an investigational corticotropin-releasing factor type 2 receptor (CRF2) peptide agonist and a potential first-in-class therapy for obesity. The Phase 1 study initially will evaluate the safety and tolerability of single ascending doses of NBIP-'2118 compared to placebo in healthy-weight adult participants, as well as those who are overweight or obese.

catalyst_text: Presented positive two year pediatric Phase 3 data
detailed_catalyst_text: New two-year results from the Phase 3 CAHtalyst Pediatric study in classic congenital adrenal hyperplasia were presented at the Pediatric Endocrine Society 2026 Annual Meeting. The data showed durable androgen control with sustained reductions in ACTH and 17-OHP alongside lower glucocorticoid doses, plus improvements in BMI and insulin resistance in children and adolescents.
catalyst_text_evidence: SAN DIEGO, 2026-05-01 /PRNewswire/ -- Neurocrine Biosciences, Inc. (NASDAQ:NBIX) today announced the presentation of new two-year data from the Phase 3 CAHtalyst Pediatric study demonstrating durable androgen control, sustained decreases in glucocorticoid (GC) doses and meaningful improvements in clinical outcomes associated with excess androgens and long-term GC exposure in children and adolescents with classic congenital adrenal hyperplasia treated with CRENESSITY (crinecerfont). These data build upon previously reported one-year clinical outcomes results and were presented at the Pediatric Endocrine Society 2026 Annual Meeting in San Francisco. Consistent with these findings, patients with classic congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH) continued to experience substantial reductions in adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) and 17-hydroxyprogesterone (17-OHP) while achieving lower, more physiologic GC doses.

catalyst_text: Presented positive two year Phase 3 CAH results
detailed_catalyst_text: Two-year data from the Phase 3 CAHtalyst Adult study were presented, showing sustained and substantial reductions in glucocorticoid dosing in adults with classic congenital adrenal hyperplasia, with about 70% reaching physiologic-range doses by month 24. Results were shared at a major endocrinology meeting and reported no new safety signals, supporting durable efficacy and long-term tolerability.
catalyst_text_evidence: Neurocrine Biosciences, Inc. (NASDAQ:NBIX) today announced the first presentation of new two-year data from the Phase 3 CAHtalyst Adult study demonstrating sustained, substantial reductions in glucocorticoid (GC) doses in adults with classic congenital adrenal hyperplasia treated with CRENESSITY, with approximately 70% of patients achieving GC doses within the physiologic range. These data build upon previously reported one-year results and were presented at the American Association of Clinical Endocrinology 2026 Annual Meeting in Las Vegas. At Month 24 of the study, 69% (103/149) of participants achieved a physiologic GC dose (≤11 mg/m2/day hydrocortisone equivalents) ... Long‑term treatment with CRENESSITY was generally well tolerated, with more than 80% study retention at two years and no new safety signals observed.

catalyst_text: Presented positive real world data showing higher persistence
detailed_catalyst_text: New real-world claims results were presented showing adults with tardive dyskinesia who initiated INGREZZA had significantly higher six-month treatment persistence and lower switching versus AUSTEDO XR. Median time to discontinuation or switch was not reached for INGREZZA (>180 days) versus 129 days for the comparator. These data reinforce durable real-world use in the approved indication and may inform treatment selection.
catalyst_text_evidence: Neurocrine Biosciences, Inc. (Nasdaq: NBIX) today announced the presentation of new real-world evidence demonstrating that adult patients with tardive dyskinesia receiving INGREZZA (valbenazine) capsules showed higher treatment persistence compared to those on AUSTEDO XR (deutetrabenazine). The findings are being presented at the Academy of Managed Care Pharmacy 2026 Annual Meeting in Nashville. Over a six-month follow-up period, patients treated with INGREZZA demonstrated statistically greater treatment continuation and lower switching rates than those receiving AUSTEDO XR. Significantly more patients persisted with their initial TD therapy in the cohort who started on INGREZZA (55.6%) compared to those who started on AUSTEDO XR (48.1%). Switching to another TD therapy at any time during the follow-up period was significantly less frequent in the INGREZZA cohort (7.7%) compared to AUSTEDO XR (11.2%). The median time to discontinuation or switch from the initial therapy was 129 days for the AUSTEDO XR cohort, while the median was not reached for the INGREZZA cohort (>180 days), indicating significantly longer time to discontinuation or switch.

catalyst_text: Presented positive post hoc analysis demonstrating meaningful improvements
detailed_catalyst_text: A post-hoc analysis from the Phase 4 KINECT-PRO study in adults aged 65 years and older with tardive dyskinesia was presented at a long-term care medical conference. The analysis showed clinically meaningful, patient-reported improvements in symptoms, quality of life, and functional impairment, with TDIS scores exceeding the threshold for meaningful change. These results support treatment decisions for older adults, including those in long-term care settings.
catalyst_text_evidence: Findings were presented at the Society for Post-Acute and Long-Term Care Medical Association (PALTmed) PALTC26 Annual Conference in Anaheim, Calif. The company also presented a first-of-its-kind post-hoc analysis from the KINECT‑PRO study demonstrating meaningful improvements in patient‑reported tardive dyskinesia (TD) impact among adults aged 65 years and older treated with INGREZZA (valbenazine) capsules. In adults aged 65 and older, once-daily INGREZZA was associated with robust patient-reported improvements in TD symptoms, quality of life and functional impairment at Week 24. Patient-reported outcomes also demonstrated reduced social and emotional burden, with improvements in total TDIS scores exceeding the established threshold for clinically meaningful change.

catalyst_text: Initiated Phase 2 trial in tardive dyskinesia patients
detailed_catalyst_text: Announced initiation of a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 2 study in approximately 100 adults with tardive dyskinesia. The trial evaluates efficacy, safety, and tolerability, with change in AIMS dyskinesia total score at Week 8 as the primary endpoint. This represents advancement of a next-generation VMAT2 inhibitor into mid-stage development for TD.
catalyst_text_evidence: Neurocrine Biosciences, Inc. (NASDAQ:NBIX) today announced the initiation of its Phase 2 clinical study of investigational compound NBI-1065890 in adults with tardive dyskinesia (TD). This Phase 2, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study will enroll approximately 100 adult subjects with TD and will assess the efficacy, safety, and tolerability of NBI-1065890 compared with placebo. The primary efficacy endpoint is change from baseline in the Abnormal Involuntary Movement Scale (AIMS) dyskinesia total score (sum of Items 1–7) at Week 8.

catalyst_text: Announced negative topline results in Phase 3 trial
detailed_catalyst_text: Topline results from the Phase 3 KINECT-DCP study in pediatric and adult participants with dyskinetic cerebral palsy showed the trial did not meet its primary or key secondary endpoints assessing improvement in chorea. Adverse events were generally consistent with the known safety profile. This is significant given the lack of approved treatments for chorea in this population and may impact further development in this indication.
catalyst_text_evidence: SAN DIEGO, 2025-12-22 /PRNewswire/ -- Neurocrine Biosciences, Inc. (NASDAQ:NBIX) today announced that its Phase 3 KINECT®-DCP study evaluating the efficacy, safety, and tolerability of valbenazine in pediatric and adult participants who have dyskinetic cerebral palsy (DCP) did not meet primary or key secondary endpoints. Adverse events were generally consistent with the established safety profile for valbenazine.
